page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-80xCPU-512GB is a Cloud Native family server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9354 processor with 80 physical cores and 80 vCPUs, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and each core has 1.0 thread. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 6.4 GB of memory per core. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core and single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, including physics, encryption, and extended instructions. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is also in the top 10% for both read and write operations, although the PassMark memory score falls into the average category. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI, which contribute to its top-tier performance in software compilation and ray tracing.

While the server excels in multi-threaded decompression and Redis SET operations, it exhibits certain performance limitations. Text generation using a medium 7B LLM model is weak, falling into the bottom 25%, and no data is available for large 70B model text generation. The shared CPU allocation presents a potential resource contention tradeoff compared to dedicated instances. Given the high core count and substantial memory capacity, this server is suited for database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
